successors.name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
successors.text: the Tai north-west of Vietnam: Lai Châu, Điện Biên (Muang Thaeng) and Sơn La; the page names the region ('the northwest') and no frontier

ledger.x: c. 1600: the Tai alliance of the north-west. The page says 'the alliance has been formalized since at least the 17th century' and the infobox 'Established: before 17th century'; Tai peoples settled the north-west 'since the early first millennium CE or, at the latest, the fifth to eighth century'. 1600 is a…
December 1953: the Viet Minh attack Lai Chau.
July 1954: the Tai Federation is dissolved.

wars.name: Haw wars on the Tai north-west (1887)
wars.outcome: In 1887 Deo Van Tri's soldiers 'together with Chinese Black Flag Army soldiers, sacked Luang Phrabang'; Pavie allied with Deo Van Tri and France recognised him as leader in 1890; no border change in the pages.

wars.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu (Tai Federation)
wars.outcome: Viet Minh attack Lai Chau in December 1953; Deo Van Un dies at Dien Bien Phu in March-May 1954; Geneva (July 1954) gives the region to the DRV.

certainty.note: A federation of Tai chiefdoms with tributes to several overlords; no frontier, area or canton list on the pages.
